title: Beyond Fail-to-Pass: Iterative Hardening of Co-Generated Bug Reproduction Tests and Fixes
datasets: SWT-Bench Verified ∩ SWE-bench Verified: 433 Python issue tasks with golden fixes and golden BRTs.
SWT-Bench Lite ∩ SWE-bench Lite: 276 Python issue tasks for cross-benchmark evaluation.

Standalone BRT injection study uses published prediction sets from LogicStar, e-Otter++, AssertFlip and OpenHands BRT-only on SWT-Bench; 1,104 F→P and 474 non-F→P instance/BRT pairs after harness-error exclusions.
task: Study whether generated bug reproduction tests help repair, measure their repair-constraining quality against plausible-but-incorrect mutation patches (Mutation Patch Evaluation), and co-generate/harden a bug test and fix through CoHarden.
input_setting: Issue report + buggy Python repo. Standalone analysis tests generated BRT against golden fix/test and semantic mutants of the golden fix (post-hoc measurement). CoHarden Phase 0 writes a user-visible witness test before any fix; hardening rounds jointly refine test and fix, mutate each current fix, and compare the current test against the previous-round test with a Temporal Matrix (no golden artifacts inside the loop).
author_artifact_url: Project page: https://aka.ms/CoHarden (redirects to https://yhtan777.github.io/CoHarden-project-page/). The page shows a disabled “Code under review” button and no source/data link.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper names the CoHarden project page. Following the official aka.ms URL reaches a project page hosted by first author Yuhao Tan’s GitHub Pages account. Page explicitly marks the GitHub code button “Code under review” with `is-disabled`; its only external URLs are site styling/favicon resources. Exact-title GitHub/code search found no public CoHarden repository. Thus implementation is not publicly released at audit time.
source_commit_or_archive: No code, prompts archive, prediction logs, immutable commit, or data package located. Official project page states “Code under review” and provides no enabled source link. SWT/SWE-bench data are public dependencies, not CoHarden source/artifact.
license: arXiv manuscript CC BY 4.0; no software/data license verified because the implementation is unavailable.
exact_models: Main CoHarden implementation: OpenHands SDK + GPT-5-mini-0807; K=5 hardening rounds, four semantic mutation operators, N=3 each (up to 12 mutations/round), τ=0.2.
Cross-backbone experiment: GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.5. Reported average cost per instance $6.69 and $18.07 respectively; GPT-5-mini main run $0.84/instance.
Standalone MPE mutation-patch generation: Agentless pipeline with GPT-5-mini; five operators, N=56/operator (280 patches/instance). OpenHands fix agent uses GPT-5-mini-0807.
weights_status: No fine-tuning or local weights; hosted commercial GPT-5-mini-0807, GPT-5.4, and Claude Opus 4.5 APIs. Exact API snapshots not further pinned beyond model-name strings. No calls made.
evaluation_route: Read all 15,387 extracted words of arXiv v1 including main paper and Appendices A–D/prompts. Main benchmark is 433 SWE-bench Verified ∩ SWT-Bench Verified tasks, with 276-task Lite intersection; metrics jointly check Resolved via SWE-bench golden tests and F→P via SWT-Bench golden tests. MPE mutates golden fixes with vanilla, symptom suppression, incomplete-fix, input-specific shortcut and behavior-substitution operators; generated test is Rigorous/Lax/Misaligned by comparison to golden BRT, with median laxity threshold τ=0.202. Standalone results: Rigorous injected tests +8.5 pp Resolved vs no-BRT; Lax +0.0 pp; Misaligned −3.6 pp. CoHarden: 69.4% Resolved/78.9% F→P, versus same-backbone OpenHands+Cogen 61.4%/72.7%; GPT-5.4/Opus 4.5 runs reach 76.2%/78.7% Resolved. No code/API execution. Project code currently under review, so result cannot be independently reproduced from a public implementation.
blockers: Official project page’s GitHub button is disabled and explicitly says “Code under review”; no author implementation, exact code snapshot, run outputs, or prediction files are public.

No available source to inspect/run the OpenHands PluggableCritic integration, mutation-patch generators, Docker harness changes, or prompts; reproducing would require implementing the method, which is not authorized.

The benchmark data are public, but the large-scale MPE analysis relies on gold patches/tests and GPT-generated mutation patches (280 candidate mutants per issue); no cached per-instance evidence is public.
Hosted API models and model snapshots are not fully frozen; cost is material: GPT-5-mini $0.84/instance, GPT-5.4 $6.69/instance, Opus 4.5 $18.07/instance. No model calls made.
concept_fit: Extremely high for oracle quality and repair-guiding tests. It distinguishes tests that merely reproduce a symptom (Lax) from tests that reject plausible incorrect fixes (Rigorous), and identifies common test–fix error coupling. Explicitly uses root-cause-oriented mutations (incomplete fix, symptom suppression, input-specific shortcut, behavior substitution), with examples grounded in a SymPy issue. It is not a root-cause taxonomy/classifier; its central contribution is a test-quality and co-hardening loop. Strong direct prior work for semantic/causal test adequacy and independent oracle assessment.
recommendation: Promote as the strongest conceptual comparator for tests that constrain a fix to the real bug/root cause, and for distinguishing symptom reproduction from adequate behavioral assertions. Its benchmark directly intersects SWE/SWT-Bench Verified and the result is unusually aligned with avoiding false or lax oracles. Do not select as an immediately reproducible baseline while official code is under review. Pair with #47 TestPrune for an available source-backed base; DPIAgent (#48) supplies explicit diagnosis handoff, while CoHarden contributes test-rigor/fix-coupling metrics.
